text:
maria: FYI: got an SLA alert from acme about 99th pct latency spikes starting ~11:20 UTC. Digging into pool shared-gpu-4.

maria: here's the initial flame: spikes coincide with a single tenant (tenant-acme) that sends lots of short 64-token requests.

sam: can you paste the metric link?

maria: https://mon.example.com/d/xyz/shared-gpu-4?orgId=1 live link + screenshot in thread. 99p shot from ~120ms -> 1.1s.

monitoring-bot: Alert: latency_99p("shared-gpu-4") > 800ms for 3m (since 1784999940)

lee: any kernel flips around that time? my quick check shows kernel_selector toggled from aten_fast -> aten_general a few times.

maria: yes, saw autoswitch logs. suspect batching heuristic oscillation. tenant-acme's bursty tiny requests make batch size borderline and the selector flips to a slower general kernel which has worse small-batch perf.

ash: do we have kv cache hit-rate for that tenant? small requests shouldn't evict much, but if kernel swap changes memory layout it could cause KV flushes.

dina: KV stats for tenant-acme between 11:15-11:30: hit_rate drops from 92% -> 60% when the kernel flips. I can attach the query I ran: 

```
SELECT time, kv_hit_rate, kernel_version FROM runtime.metrics
WHERE pool='shared-gpu-4' AND tenant='tenant-acme' AND time >= '2026-03-17T11:00:00Z' AND time < '2026-03-17T11:40:00Z'
ORDER BY time;
```

maria: thanks. So chain is: small batch pattern -> selector misclassifies as needing aten_general -> kernel switch triggers full rebind/recompiles for active model variant -> KV cache pointer reshuffle -> hot cache misses -> token latency spike.

sam: can we reproduce locally? maybe a loadgen with same QPS and request size. I can spin one in dev-gpu-1.

lee: also saw an increase in compile_time metric during spike window. compile_time p95 went from 40ms -> 600ms.

ash: ops-bot, can you temporarily pin tenant-acme to kernel=aten_fast on shared-gpu-4 for 30m? Need to confirm if that reduces latency.

ops-bot: @ash executing: set-tenant-config --tenant tenant-acme --pool shared-gpu-4 --kernel aten_fast --ttl 1800s

ops-bot: done. change propagated to control plane at 1785000022.

maria: after pin, 99p dropped to ~150ms within 90s. Looks promising.

dina: plotted KV hit_rate — back to 91% after change. Good sign.

sam: reproduced locally with loadgen: when kernel flipping enabled we see compile churn + KV miss. With kernel pinned it's stable.

lee: root cause appears to be selector threshold logic: it uses recent batch-size histogram but the estimator has high variance for small-window low-latency bursts; it trips to general kernel to favor long sequences but our tenant produces lots of short sequences. The cost estimation penalty for switching is underestimated.

ash: short-term fix: add a hysteresis to selector (min dwell time 60s) and increase cost_of_switch penalty by x3 for shared pools. Also add a special-case for tenants with median_seq_len < 80 to prefer aten_fast.

sam: I can open a PR for hysteresis + config flag; will add integration test that simulates bursty small requests.

maria: action items:
- sam: PR + unit tests (ETA 1 day)
- lee: ensure compile_time logs are tagged with tenant and kernel (ETA 2d)
- dina: run KV eviction replay for tenant-acme to verify no residual corruption (ETA today)
- ash: add temporary telemetry dashboard for selector flips per-tenant (ETA 4h)

ash: noted. I'll also run a small job to scan other shared pools for similar tenants.

dina: logging note: we should record "selector_decision_reason" in trace for next rollout. will add to backlog.

maria: I'll follow up with acme CS to explain mitigation and ETA.

sam: ping me if you need the loadgen scripts.

maria: thanks everyone. marking as investigating -> mitigated. Will reopen if we see recurrence. :white_check_mark:
